hook timeouts: named verdicts, not swallowed exits

Issue #4087, the last || true of the #4085 sweep. run_hook_with_input in tests/unit/test-image-paste-guard.sh ran timeout N node ... 2>/dev/null || true, so when the per-hook budget killed node (exit 124) the exit code was thrown away and the empty output was fed to the assertions as if it were a hook verdict. Drag the two knobs to see what each line of the suite printed before and after the fix.

Inputs

1.0s
150ms
Presets:

What the runner did


    


    

      
Before: || true swallowed the exit code

      

      


      
After: rc 124 is its own verdict

      

      

    

  


  

    
The rules the fix bakes in

    
rc 0      -> pass the hook's stdout through, the assertions judge the real verdict
rc 124    -> stdout becomes the literal ERROR token, stderr names the cause:
             hook '<name>' timed out after Ns (ORK_HOOK_TIMEOUT); no verdict was produced
other rc  -> pass stdout through unchanged (out of scope here, same as #4086)

    

      ERROR fails every assertion shape in this file (it is neither JSON nor silent success), so a timeout can
      never read as PASS, and the cause line sits right above the FAIL line instead of two layers away. The
      verdict is echoed rather than log_fail'ed because callers capture the helper's stdout inside
      $( ): a counter increment there would run in a subshell and never reach the summary. The
      shape is the one #4086 gave hook_decision; the hanging hook that proves it lives in the new
      "Hook budget" section of the suite, which fakes a never-answering runner under a 1 s budget.
    

  


  

    
What the fix answers (measured 2026-09-13, QA)

    

      
casebeforeafter

      
        

          hook exceeds ORK_HOOK_TIMEOUT
          empty output, verdict line says a wrong PASS or FAIL, nothing names the timeout (3 cases at a 2 s hook with ORK_HOOK_TIMEOUT=1)
          ERROR verdict plus "timed out after Ns (ORK_HOOK_TIMEOUT)"
        

        

          latency test with both runs killed
          both deltas read ~0, the perf assertion PASSES on a dead hook
          stderr names the timeout for each killed run
        

        

          healthy hook
          unchanged
          unchanged (25/25 with the budget path exercised)
        

      
    

    

      No assertion was weakened and no default was raised. The residual 100 ms stdin-watchdog shape from #4085
      needs no handling here: this file feeds the hook through a builtin echo, whose bytes are already in the
      pipe before node spawns, so the watchdog has no producer-side boot to race.
